messages.author: 17f8070912132195
messages.subject: Re: Link two proportional data
parts:
I checked the package "dirinla", but it doesn't allow a composition data as predictor.

On Wednesday, November 8, 2023 at 9:31:22 PM UTC-6 Ruby Ji wrote:
Hi all,

I have two sets of proportional data (x and y).  I want to link them via a simple regression: log(y_s,t) = a + b * log(x_s,t), where y_s,t is a proportions in s-th site and t-th time,  x_s,t is another proportions in s-th site and t-th time. And, y_1,s,t + y_2,s,t + y_3,s,t = 1, and the same for x_s,t.

Currently, I am fitting a separate model for each group except the last one:
log(y_1,s,t) = a_1 + b_1 * log(x_1,s,t), and get est_y_1,s,t
log(y_2,s,t) = a_2 + b_2 * log(x_2,s,t), and get est_y_2,s,t
est_y_3,s,t = 1- est_y_1,s,t - est_y_2,s,t

Is there a way to control the predictor within (0,1), or model these proportions together?

Thanks,
Ruby

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Link two proportional data
parts:
Hi Rujia,

Thank you for your comment.

The implementation allows the use of all the latent fields implemented in R-INLA. Additionally, it allows for the effect to be shared, shared and scaled, or replicated.

In the example in the paper, a continuous spatial effect with Matérn covariance is used, but you could also include a temporal effect, or a combination of both.

Best,

Joaquín
